aggregation: Median run-level successful p95, useful throughput and job counts; pooled rejection percentages and error counts. Whiskers show min/max of three repeats, not confidence intervals. Job counts include drain; job production stops when the HTTP load command returns, including its response tail.
comparison: Combined contention signal plus existing server-owned workload-class sharing versus retained occupancy-only policy. Not an ablation or proof that either change alone produces the result.
limitations: Short local workload, no admission queue, no preemption or starvation bound. Initial detection requires a new pool wait after provider construction; historical totals are ignored. Full-after-wait remains pressured until nonfull/quiet. A pressure cap1 and critical reservation1 still block background under real contention. These workload classes use the tenant dimension, not an additional independent customer isolation layer.
